title: Probabilistic Prefill Acceptor: latency-first routing, kernel fallthrough, and graceful rollback
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement a lightweight probabilistic "early acceptor" that validates partial prefill outputs to enable a latency-first speculative path. The acceptor uses a combined score from model-level confidence, kernel execution affinity, and recent acceptance statistics to either commit a prefilling shard early or fall through to the standard decode path with kernel fallback. This reduces median latency for short responses while bounding cost and preserving output quality.
background: We currently support speculative paths that rely on full prefill probes and multi-model handoffs. Those mechanisms reduce tail latency but are expensive when probes often fail to produce an acceptable early output. Recent customer telemetry shows a high proportion of sub-64-token requests where early acceptance would yield large latency wins. We need a cheaper, probabilistic validator that trades modest quality uncertainty for consistent latency improvements with clear fallback behavior.
goals: 1) Reduce P50 latency for requests <=64 tokens by 20% for supported models. 2) Keep early-accept false-positive rate under 1% on evaluation prompts. 3) Ensure graceful, observable fallback to canonical decode with kernel-level fallthrough when acceptor signals uncertainty or kernel mismatch.
non_goals: 1) Global redesign of routing layer. 2) Replacing full speculative multi-model hedging. 3) Addressing long-form generation optimizations in this ticket.
design_overview: The acceptor lives in the prefill scheduling stage as an optional post-prefill validator. Key components: (a) Local scoring function combining softmax confidence proxy, token-level consistency heuristics, and recency-weighted acceptance rate; (b) Kernel affinity classifier that emits a compatibility score for committing on the current kernel vs requiring fallthrough; (c) Decision policy with tri-state outcomes: ACCEPT, REJECT, or DEFER. ACCEPT triggers early commit and returns streaming tokens. REJECT triggers immediate fallback to canonical decode. DEFER continues with the normal decode handoff. All decisions emit tagged telemetry and a small decision trace to the console for debugging.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Automated eval harness shows <=1% degradation in BLEU/ROUGE-equivalent quality metrics on curated prompt set for accepted early outputs. 2) Canary rollout demonstrates >=20% P50 latency reduction for <=64-token traffic on runtime-2.1. 3) No more than 0.5% of requests experience double-execution (duplicate charge) during steady-state. 4) Telemetry shows decision flags and kernel affinity metrics present in Console dashboards.
implementation_steps: 1) Prototype scoring function and kernel-affinity classifier behind a feature flag. 2) Add decision-layer interface in prefill scheduler and wire three outcomes into runtime paths. 3) Implement a per-request circuit-breaker that disables early acceptor after X consecutive misaccepts. 4) Instrument tags, counters, and sampling traces. 5) Run offline eval and A/B canary. 6) Roll out staged by model family and region.
telemetry_and_metrics: Emit these instruments: acceptor_decision{ACCEPT|REJECT|DEFER}, acceptor_confidence_score (histogram), kernel_affinity_score (histogram), early_accept_false_positive (counter), early_accept_true_positive (counter), acceptor_invocations (counter), double_execution_events (counter). Dashboards: acceptance-rate by model, P50/P95 latency delta for accepted vs baseline, cost-per-token delta for accepted path, per-kernel acceptance heatmap.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal lab tests and offline eval (1 week). Phase 1: Canary 1% traffic for non-sensitive tenant group A (2 weeks). Monitor acceptance-rate and double-exec. Phase 2: Expand to 10% across regions with per-model opt-out (2 weeks). Phase 3: Full rollout with throttled concurrency and autoscaling knobs. Gate expansion on telemetry SLAs.
rollback_plan: Immediate rollback via feature flag if double_execution_events > 0.5% of accepted requests over 1-hour window or if early_accept_false_positive rate exceeds 1% on live traffic. Fallback: disable acceptor and revert to canonical decode scheduler; run rollback-runbook to reconcile partial outputs and billing anomalies.
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring math and kernel-affinity classifier. Integration tests simulating model mixes and kernel mismatches. E2E via harness with sampled real prompts to verify no regressions in output quality. Load test to verify acceptor does not become throughput bottleneck and that circuit-breaker triggers appropriately.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False accepts degrade quality for high-value customers. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds; per-tenant opt-outs. Risk: Kernel affinity misclassification causes wasted compute. Mitigation: prefer DEFER over ACCEPT when affinity below safe threshold and default to REJECT rather than ACCEPT if mismatch detected. Risk: Telemetry leakage of PII in traces. Mitigation: sampled traces must be scrubbed and reviewed by Security.
